text:
Maya C.: Heads-up: seeing ~3% NDCG drop on canary after candidate-sharding rollout (~50% traffic). Quick numbers and repro below.
Jonathan: Ugh. Which slice? overall or short queries? link: https://dash.redwood.internal/ndcg?run=3509
Maya C.: Short queries (<= 10 tokens) and mixed-length docs. MRR pretty flat, NDCG shifts top-heavy. Sample: baseline=0.612 -> canary=0.593
Srini: Sounds like candidate imbalance from sharding. If a few partitions have fewer high-quality negatives, top-k distribution changes.
Eva: Also check candidate serialization/truncation — we had a proto-change last week that pads passages differently. Could affect scoring ordering.
Maya C.: Repro steps I used:
1) deploy canary with SHARDING=true
2) run rankbench --cohort shortqueries --candidates 250 --seed 42
3) compute ndcg@10 and mrr
Log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T17:22:03Z rerank: candidates_loaded=250 shards=5 shard_id=3
2026-03-15T17:22:03Z score: top1=0.768 top10_avg=0.612
```
Jonathan: Can you dump candidate id distribution per shard? I want to see if specific shards are missing high-quality candidates.
Maya C.: Yup. Attached counts (quick): shard0:250k, shard1:253k, shard2:249k, shard3:190k, shard4:248k — shard3 looks small
Srini: There you go. If shard3 is underpopulated it's effectively reducing candidate diversity for queries routed there.
Eva: Why is shard3 small? Deployment config maybe used a different selector — last change replaced consistent-hash with mod(hash) for speed.
Maya C.: @deploy-bot rolled that change on Mar 12th during perf tuning. deploy-bot: "change: candidate-router -> use fast modulus hash; rolled to canary at 2026-03-12T09:04Z"
Srini: Modulus hash can cluster if keyspace not uniform. Quick math: if doc IDs are sequential from some source, mod can create skew.
Jonathan: Short-term mitigation: revert to consistent-hash or add manual rebalancing bucket assignment. Long-term: add sampling-based sanity in rankbench to detect shard skew.
Maya C.: Quick experiments I ran:
- revert hash -> ndcg back to 0.611 (within noise)
- keep mod(hash) but increase candidate pool to 400 -> ndcg 0.608 (partial recovery)
Eva: Good. Also verify tokenization parity between candidate pipeline and reranker encoder. If shards serve differently-tokenized text that could change top-k too.
Maya C.: Checked tokenization: same tokenizer binary, but candidate serialization truncates to 512 words vs 512 tokens. Oops.
Srini: That explains short-query sensitivity. For short queries, which rely on top few signals, truncation discrepancies can flip ranking.
Jonathan: OK action items:
- Maya: revert mod(hash) in canary and run 10k-sample shadow A/B to confirm (owner: Maya)
- Srini: add a small diagnostic in rankbench to report per-shard candidate quality (top1 frequency, avg score)
- Eva: patch candidate serializer to use token-based truncation and add unit test
- Infra: schedule a canary-only reindex for shard3 after rebalancing
Maya C.: I'll start the revert now and run the sample. If we still see >2% NDCG drop after revert, we'll rollback fully.
Jonathan: Nice triage. Also add a quick dashboard alert for sudden shard-size deltas so we catch these earlier :thumbsup:
Eva: I'll open the PR for token-truncation today.
deploy-bot: "deploy: candidate-router reverted to consistent-hash on canary at 2026-03-15T17:33Z (by Maya C.)"
Maya C.: Repro run started; ETA ~20min. Will post results.
Jonathan: Thanks — ping here when done.
